full_judgment: 32. In the case, S.M.S. Samity Vs. Bangladesh 39 DLR (AD) 85 relied upon by Mr. Asrarul Hossain all the above decisions were considered and distinction was made between an (1) ordinary contract and (2) a contract in exercise of a statutory or executive or sovereign power of the state. It was then held that a contract assuming the characteristics of the latter class is enforceable by the court in its writ jurisdiction. In the cited case; it was found that provisions had been made for leasing out fisheries and lands by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, and various rules were framed thereunder for entering into contract of lease and when the petitioner sought to enforce by writ petition such a contract of lease of a fishery given to it but subsequently cancelled and then given to another person, it was held that the said contract having been entered into by the Government in performance of its functions under statutory rules was enforceable by the court in its writ jurisdiction.
